article.articleTextExcerpt: Six persons were killed and seven others sustained injuries after a truck transporting wheat rammed into a stationary mini goods vehicle on a highway in Chhattisgarh's Balod district on Friday, police said. The accident occurred around 11.30 am at Markatola Ghat, under Purur police station limits, on National Highway-30, when the victims, members of a 'dhumal' music band, were travelling towards Jagdalpur from Kabirdham district, an official said. He said that the goods vehicle, carrying 15 persons and their musical instruments, broke down at Markatola Ghat, and two of the occupants had gone to Dhamtari in search of a mechanic. A 16-wheeler truck loaded with wheat, heading towards Jagdalpur from Raipur, crashed into the stationary goods vehicle from behind. The truck dragged the vehicle about 30 metres before it overturned, the official said. Some of the victims were trapped under heavy sacks of wheat, and two of them died on the spot, while four succumbed to injuries during treatment at the Dhamtari district hospital, he said. The seven injured persons have been referred to Raipur for further treatment, the official said, adding that the truck driver fled the scene after the crash

article.title: Mono Rail Projects
article.description: Guide to monorail in India — the Mumbai Monorail (MMRDA), how straddle-beam monorail works, shelved projects and the latest news.
article.postedBy: Metro, RRTS & High-Speed Rail Project Updates
article.sourceName: Metro, RRTS & High-Speed Rail Project Updates
article.articleTextExcerpt: A monorail runs on a single elevated beam rather than a conventional two-rail track. That makes it a compact, fully elevated mode, useful on dense urban corridors where road space is tight. In India the flagship is the Mumbai Monorail, the country’s first and so far only system. This page covers monorail in India: how the technology works, where it runs, and the latest developments. A monorail vehicle straddles or hangs from a single guideway beam, usually on rubber tyres. The result is a small footprint, a tight turning radius and a quiet ride. Most modern systems, Mumbai’s included, use the straddle-beam design, where the train sits astride a slim concrete beam. On capacity it sits below metro. It works well as a feeder or on medium-demand corridors, but it cannot match a metro’s throughput, which is why cities weigh it carefully against light metro and Metrolite. The Mumbai Monorail is India’s first and only monorail, running 19.54 km between Chembur and Sant Gadge Maharaj Chowk (Jacob Circle) under the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), serving eastern and central Mumbai neighbourhoods that the metro and suburban rail do not reach directly. The study found that around 35 per cent of buildings in Shimla and 30 per cent in Kullu are located within areas identified as susceptible to landslides. Mandi recorded building exposure of about 22 per cent, followed by Solan at 21 per cent. The assessment was carried out by IIT-Mandi researchers Ankit Singh, Nitesh Dhiman, Kirti Kumar Mahanta and Dericks P Shukla, Professor of Remote Sensing at the School of Civil and Environmental Engineering. The researchers used machine-learning-based Landslide Susceptibility Maps (LSMs) to assess the likelihood of landslides across the state. Three artificial intelligence models — Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) — were employed to classify areas according to their varying levels of landslide susceptibility. article.description: The recently concluded National Family Health Survey-6 (NFHS-6) has revealed a worrying trend in Ludhiana district. It has brought forward that the proportion of households...
article.articleTextExcerpt: The recently concluded National Family Health Survey-6 (NFHS-6) has revealed a worrying trend in Ludhiana district. It has brought forward that the proportion of households consuming iodised salt has dropped from 94.9 per cent in the last survey to 88.7 per cent. Iodised salt is a critical source of iodine, a trace mineral required for the production of thyroid hormones that regulate growth, metabolism and development. Public health experts warn that the decline in usage could reverse decades of progress made under India’s Universal Salt Iodisation (USI) programme, which was introduced to combat iodine deficiency disorders. The growing popularity of sendha namak (rock salt) and other speciality variants has contributed to the decline. “While these alternatives are often marketed as ‘natural’ or ‘pure’ but they lack adequate iodine content. Sendha namak may be used occasionally, but relying on it exclusively for daily cooking deprives the body of essential iodine,” said Dipti, a nutritionist. However, illegal constructions—public, commercial or religious—have encroached upon the vital spaces, reducing greenery and restricting public access. Authorities must enforce building and land-use laws uniformly without making any exceptions whatsoever. Any action should follow due legal process, with adequate notice and compliance with applicable regulations. Similarly, unauthorised boundary walls constructed in violation of bylaws—that permit a maximum height of six feet—should also get immediate attention. Such violations undermine urban planning and embolden others to ignore civic rules. The Municipal Corporation (MC) should initiate appropriate proceedings against all illegal constructions and similar violations in accordance with the law. Then came the food. Hot poha, jalebi, dhokla, Bhopali paan and Bhopali chai. Nothing extraordinary, perhaps, but sitting with my father, putting my worries aside and eating without thinking about the examination felt strangely comforting. We visited the Upper and Lower Lakes. article.articleTextExcerpt: Construction 1 min read Trichy civic body warns builders over illegal construction & demolition waste dumping The civic body will penalise builders dumping construction materials on roads and disrupting traffic in areas including Thennur and Vayalur Road, while a C&D waste recycling unit is planned at Panjapur. TNN Published On Oct 2, 2026 at 02:35 PM IST Representative AI imageTrichy Corporation Commissioner N Ponmalai on Thursday warned builders and construction companies against dumping construction and demolition (C&D) waste on roads and near water bodies, following complaints from residents that such dumping was affecting vehicular movement.The commissioner said the corporation would levy on-the-spot penalties, as per its bylaws, against those continuing to dispose of C&D waste illegally.Dumping of construction materials and debris on roads has caused traffic bottlenecks in several parts of the city, including Thennur, Vayalur Road and Uyyakondan aqueduct bund roads. The corporation also said temporary shelters for storing construction materials or accommodating workers should be confined to the private property where construction is under way and should not encroach on roads.

article.articleTextExcerpt: The long-awaited Delhi-Panipat-Karnal rapid rail project has received a fresh push with the Haryana Government formally including the corridor in its Transit Oriented Development (TOD) Policy, raising hopes among residents that work on the project will gain momentum. The Town and Country Planning Department, in a notification issued recently, amended the policy notified in 2016 to include the Delhi-Panipat-Karnal Namo Bharat Regional Rapid Transit System corridor among the Mass Rapid Transit System corridors eligible for transit-oriented development. The notification said the corridor had been approved by the state government on the recommendation of the Haryana Mass Rapid Transport Corporation. Following a request from the corporation, the alignment has now been incorporated into the annexure of the existing policy. The project was initially planned from Sarai Kale Khan in Delhi to Panipat. It was later extended to Karnal by then Chief Minister Manohar Lal Khattar in January 2020. Karnal was included in the National Capital Region in June 2015, raising expectations of improved connectivity and modern infrastructure. The demand pertains to nearly 20 acres of defence land adjacent to the hospital, which the Health Department says is required for decongesting the existing facility and undertaking proposed expansion projects. An extension block of the Civil Hospital is already under construction, but officials have maintained that additional land is essential to meet future healthcare needs in the cantonment area. The issue had earlier been highlighted by The Tribune in a report titled “Land shortage clouds Ambala Civil Hospital expansion plans” published on July 16. This is not the first time the matter has been taken up with the Defence Ministry. Vij had made a similar request last year as well, but Army authorities had reportedly expressed reservations citing security concerns and limited availability of land. article.description: A nearly 65-year-old former Sarpanch was allegedly hacked to death with an axe outside a liquor vend at Jassi Pauwali Chowk here on Sunday evening.
article.articleTextExcerpt: A nearly 65-year-old former Sarpanch was allegedly hacked to death with an axe outside a liquor vend at Jassi Pauwali Chowk here on Sunday evening. The deceased has been identified as Jagtar Singh, alias Tara, a resident of Phus Mandi village. He had reportedly gone to the liquor vend when he was attacked. According to his relatives, the deceased was first hit twice with an axe. The attacker then allegedly returned from a nearby chowk and attacked him again, and fled off. Jagtar sustained serious injuries and died. The incident took place in a public place, however, nobody came forward to intervene, the relatives of deceased claimed. Jagtar's brother said that he was not aware of any enmity involving the deceased. The police have arrested the accused, identified as Gurbaksh Singh of the Phus Mandi village, along with the weapon used to commit the crime. Bathinda SP (City) Aaswant Singh visited the spot and said the accused and the deceased had a personal enmity. Jagtar Singh is survived by a son and a daughter, both married. A case under Sections 21C, 27(a), 61 and 85 of the NDPS Act has been registered at Sadar police station, Kotkapura. Preliminary investigation suggests the duo had brought the consignment from Fazilka and Ferozepur and planned to supply it across the state. After coming to Fazilka, Abohar gradually became an important part of my official routine. article.title: Regional buzz: Turncoats have a field day
article.description: Pargat cut his political teeth with SAD and was elected as its MLA, before he switched to the Congress.
article.articleTextExcerpt: Regional buzz: Turncoats have a field dayPargat cut his political teeth with SAD and was elected as its MLA, before he switched to the Congress.Published on: Oct 5, 2026, 07:49:00 ISTBy HT CorrespondentsPrefer HTon GoogleShare viaCopy link Call it a coincidence or the revolving door of politics. With former hockey Olympian Pargat Singh’s getting the top job at Punjab Congress in the lead-up to assembly polls, three of the state’s four key parties are now led by turncoats. Pargat cut his political teeth with SAD and was elected as its MLA, before he switched to the Congress. Kewal Dhillon, who heads the BJP, has had a long inning in the Congress before turning saffron in 2022. Aam Aadmi Party’s president-senior minister Aman Arora was with the Congress before he jumped onto the AAP bandwagon. Another happenstance for the Congress is that it will be contesting its second consecutive assembly polls under a sports star-turned-politician: in 2022, ex-cricketer Navjot Sidhu was at the helm of party when it lost power to AAP.
